reading.body:
Four suppliers make up this collection, split evenly between two high-bandwidth memory makers, Micron and SK hynix, and two AI-training storage platforms, VAST Data and WekaIO.

SK hynix is named as the leading HBM supplier and NVIDIA's primary memory partner for datacenter GPUs, shipping both HBM3E and the newer HBM4, while Micron is described more narrowly as the US-based HBM supplier, with its HBM3E shipping specifically in H200 and Blackwell platforms. That framing, one company as the leading global supplier and the other identified by its national base rather than by market position, is the clearest signal in this data about how the two are positioned relative to each other.

VAST Data's entry specifically names CoreWeave as a customer whose GPU clusters run its all-flash platform, a direct link to the data center capital expenditure figures tracked elsewhere on this site, where CoreWeave's quarterly capex jumped from 1.4 billion to 7.7 billion dollars in the most recent year. WekaIO is described as a parallel filesystem for AI training I/O feeding GPU clusters at unnamed hyperscale customers, a similar role to VAST's but without a named customer in this data.
